newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt envoy toils on to break Israel-PLO impasse.
newsitem.headline: Egypt envoy toils on to break Israel-PLO impasse.

text.p: An Egyptian envoy said after separate talks on Thursday with Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu and the PLO's Yasser Arafat that more work was needed to end a Middle East peacemaking crisis.
Osama el-Baz's mediation mission was clouded by an outbreak of Israeli-Palestinian violence that ended months of relative calm in the Gaza Strip.

Palestinians said four Arabs were shot and wounded by Israeli soldiers and settlers during stone-throwing protests over the building of a fence at a Jewish outpost and a memorial ceremony for an Israeli soldier killed in violence in September.
The Israeli army said Palestinian police eventually restored order. Israel Television showed the Israeli army deployed two tanks close to one troublespot, though out of sight of Palestinians.
"We will continue with more consultations and contacts in the coming period," Baz said after meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for two hours.
"We hope this...in a positive spirit will lead to a breakthrough in the situation that would allow the peace process to be preserved," Baz told reporters in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
The Egyptian envoy met Arafat after holding two hours of talks in Tel Aviv with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

There was no sign Baz had arranged another round of deliberations between Israeli and PLO negotiators on resuming full-fledged peace talks suspended since Israel began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Egyptian mediation efforts led to talks in Cairo on Sunday between Palestinian and Israeli negotiators on restarting formal sessions. It was the first such meeting since the deadlock.
"Today's (Thursday's) meeting demonstrated that there is a gap that exists between the two sides," PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters after the Ramallah talks.
But Erekat said it was premature to jump to conclusions about the success of Baz's mission, which followed unsuccessful U.S. efforts to get Israel and the PLO talking peace again.
"We are continuing efforts...to try to resume the peace talks and stabilise the security situation," Netanyahu told reporters at the start of his meeting with Baz.
The envoy said "the most important thing is to find a formula that will be acceptable to both parties for maintaining peace and stability and tranquility in the region".
Netanyahu has denied media reports he would order a pause in the large housing project at the East Jerusalem site Israel calls Har Homa and Palestinians refer to as Jabal Abu Ghneim.
Palestinians refuse to return to substantive negotiations until Israel halts settlement activities in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Netanyahu, who after taking office a year ago lifted a partial freeze on Jewish settlement imposed by the prior dovish government he ousted in elections, says the construction does not violate peace deals.
Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and claimed the whole city as its capital in a move not recognised internationally. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state.
